The Islamic State Spreads

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As we reel in face of the recent Paris attacks we ask what does this mean for the future of Europe

Summary:
With France retaliating and attacking ISIS now how will this play out next week and how will it impact Africa.

We will be looking at ISIS from a global perspective and also at other terror groups including the work of BOKO HARAM in Nigeria, Somalia and elsewhere so that we can look at the impact of ISIS on the middle east and Europe and also how they link to terror groups like BOKO HARAM in Africa – to give a wider context.
What is the situation in Syria for refugees, we speak to someone who is planning to leave how have the Paris strikes affected them.
The recent bombings in Beirut, targeting Hizbullah area of Beirut, we interview with someone from Hizbullah about why Hizbullah is involved in Syria + threat of ISIS

The most deaths ever after the war, does this mean a world wide polarisation and World War three. How will this affect the refugee crisis, in light of the fact some of the attackers are believed to have come through as a refugee, will new laws be put in place will Europe's sympathy with these homeless travellers dry up., how will this play out with Syrian refugees

Press Release:


Global Terror Threat
In the wake of recent bloodshed in Paris, governments the world over responded to the call to unify in the fight against terrorism, from carrying out air strikes against terror bases to taking on the online communication systems used to rally sympathisers. From ISIS to Al Qaeda, Somalian jihadists al-Shabaab and Nigeria's Boko Haram, Carte Blanche investigates the networks responsible for thousands of innocent lives displaced and lost.


Script:


Link
The media focus this week has been on Paris but there has been a massive upsurge in attacks by Islamic extremists in many parts of the world with Africa being a vulnerable target.

V/O 15 sec
On Friday in Bameko, Mali gunmen stormed the Radisson Blu Hotel, taking over 170 hostages ,,,, 27 people are feared to have been killed. The Islamic miltants responsible are linked to Al Quada.

SFX Bomb Blast

15 sec
Earlier this week another two bomb attacks in 24 hours, in the Nigerian towns of Yola and Kano, around 40 people killed, over a hundred injured. Islamic extremist group Boko Haram are the prime suspect.

Martin: In the past 5 years the growth of terrorism has been exponential it has grown to a scale no one I ever imagined…

V/O 6 and a half sec
Martin Ewi, is with the Institute of Security Studies, his speciality counter terrorism.

Martin Ewi
SENIOR RESEARCHER, ISS
Transnational Threats & International Crime

Martin: Boko Harem has surpassed even the Islamic State in terms of casualties Boko Haram has killed just in 2014 6 664 people the Islamic State has killed 6 073 so you can see Boko Haram today is the most dangerous group in the world, is the deadliest.

V/O
One of the suicide bombers in the `Nigerian attacks this week was an 11 year old girl.

Martin: We have had suicide bombers as old a 9 in Cameroon a suicide bomber was 7 years old so you can imagine they are using children to carry bombs around and they have actually warned that they are now ready to use babies, babies who carry bombs and they will use them to explode where ever they want there’s absolutely no limit.




V/O
This year there has been an explosion of horrific attacks on ordinary people, ordinary citizens of the world. In Nigeria a massacre with a death toll claimed to be as high as 2000;, France the Charlie Hebdoe attacks, ; an armed assault in a hotel in Libya, an attack on a museum in Tunisia; suicide strikes in a Shite mosque in Yemen, an embassy explosion in Egypt; a bombing of a Peace Rally in Turkey; the downing of a Russian Plane in the Sinai, a double suicide bombing in Lebanon……to name just the major terrorist hits..

V/O 14sec
The three main terrorist groups are Boko Haram, based in North Eastern Nigeria; Al Shabaab operating out of East Africa and the Islamic State with its strongholds in North Eastern Syria

Martin: There are a lot of links amongst these terrorist groups we normally refer to them as a global network because they talk amongst themselves, share intelligence, and that’s the danger to the international community.

V/O 17 sec
Na’eem Jeenah is the executive director of the Afro- Middle East Centre. His fascination is with the rise of the Islamic State Group or ISIS… which originally started as an affiliate of Al Quada because of the American Invasion of Iraq in 2003

Na’eem: Even at that time and in that period it was regarded in Al Quada circles as being more more brutal than necessary which is saying something.

V/O 12 sec
In 2013, ISIS left Iraq to start an Al Quada branch in Syria but the two groups fell out mainly because of their different strategies.

Na'eem Jeenah
Executive Director, Afro-Middle East Centre

Al Quada strategy was to serve as a base for people from different parts of the world they would come there get there military and ideological training and go back and do their thing…. ISIS has a different way in which it operates it’s strategy is to capture and hold territory and create political entity.

Paula: The ultimate goal of Islamic State is global expansion you just need to look at the name it used to be ISIS Islamic State in Iraq and Syria and now we are talking about Islamic State they dropped the Iraq and Syria

V/O 15 sec
Paula Slier is the middle East bureau chief for Russia today, she also reports for Carte Blanche. Paula covers conflict zones and crises which makes her some what of a specialist on the Islamic State Group. We crossed over to the Tel Aviv Studio

Paula Slier
Middle East Bureau Chief : Russia Today
Tel Aviv Studio

Paula: The organisation really sees itself as persecuting what it calls the infidels and the way organisation sees itself as building the global caliphate through global jihad,

Derek: Now you talk about a caliphate what is the difference between that and a Muslim country which there are many?
Na’eem: A caliphate would have the allegiance of all Muslims around the world not within a particular nation state.

Martin: They know the interest of many of the young people so they will target them you’re talking of twitter face book, its a big appeal for young people the issue of free sex if you’re in this caliphate you can have sex and children get married at age of 9.
Derek: Isn’t that against Islam?
Martin: Absolutely against Islam but they cover it by saying Jihad if it is Jihad things you can do to reach the end this is why I am saying it want defeats reason.

Link
What is frightening is the change in tactics of Islamic state...they used to rely on lone wolf followers to strike western targets, but now it seems the attacks are finely planned and choreographed.

Na’eem: The Islamic State is pretty good at the way it undertakes its operation part of the reason for this is it’s military hierarchy is dominated by officers that were previously in Saddam Hussein’s army who are now running the military strategy for ISIS and that’s why we’ve seen so many victories they have had on the ground.

Derek: Do you think we underrate the power of the Islamic State the finances the resources they’ve got?
N’eemm:. Certainly financial it has huge resources the Islamic State sells oil on the open market and makes a lot of money from oil. They control territory where they regard people there as their citizens and they tax them like any state does. When they took over Mosul and other places in Iraq they raided banks and took possession of gold and foreign currency.

Martin: Isis is the biggest it is the richest terrorist group today on earth, its gong to take years to eliminate ISIS>

6 mins 51 sec

BREAK HERE

Link
A day before the night of terror in Paris, Beirut was attacked, a double suicide bombing that ripped through a busy street at rush hour...over 40 people were killed

V/O 9 sec
And the heartbreaking stories like that of 3 year old Haider Moustafa who lost both his parents in the blasts, were never touched on…

Martin: One was under reported the other well reported the Beirut attack very few people knew about, the media did not do it justice in terms of reporting it and the Paris attack of course woke up the whole world

Link
Within 24 hours of the Paris attacks articles began circulating on social media about a massacre at Garissa university in Kenya. what was really strange is that this carnage actually took place seven months ago

V/O
Nearly 7 million people clicked on the headline that said Kenyan University attack kills 147

Martin: If you link it to an already popular event like the Paris attacks you say of by the way in in Africa there was this attack in Kenya of course the whole world which is watch what is happening in Paris will say in Africa there is also this phenomena and they will click on it

V/O
Islamist gun men, part of the Al- Shabaab militant group, burst into the University before dawn, taking hostages and killing over 140 and its not the only terrorist attacks this country has had to deal with.

Martin: Kenya has suffered some of bloodiest terrorist attacks on continent
Martin I think what is critical is the way country responds to an attack we have seen with some African attacks government do not show seriousness for example when it happened in France, Francois Hollande was very quick and he condemned PIX Francois
Derek: So their leaders not as categorical.
Martin: Our leaders sometimes do not take things as seriously.

V/O 10 sec
A case in point, In January this year just before Paris’s Charlie Hebdo attack, Baga, a small town in Nigeria was attacked by Boko Haram militants. It was a massacre.

Martin: 2000 died in the Boko Haram attacks// 12 people died in the Paris attack in January but how many people did know about the attacks in Baga, very few but everyone knew that Paris was attacked, why because of responses of the two governments the Nigerian government took days to even acknowledge what was going on in Baga when you respond like this you can’t expect the press to do your own job.

V/O
Post Paris how will the border be policed… how will we ensure the integrity of a refugee… …Is Islamaphobia on the rise.

Derek: There is a viewpoint the Muslim population could be more outspoken and could take more action against extremists.
Na’eem: Muslims are becoming increasingly tired of every time there is an attack they are asked to condemn it. …I refuse to say not in my name what they do is not in my name…. I would condemn as I would condemn atrocities any where else these are human rights violations not because they are Muslim and I happen to be Muslim.

Martin: if you want to fight these groups you need Muslims you need Christians you need everyone on board. We want the whole world to stand up against these groups.

V/O
This year alone, its been estimated that over 750 000 refugees have been detected at the European Union borders, and that’s just those detected, not counting refugees who are under the radar.

Link
The conflict in Syria has been the biggest driver of refugees to Europe...but how will the attitudes towards the migrants change after the Paris attacks

V/O
Very likely because what has been widely reported is that two of the attackers came through the refugee camps

Paula: There was a Syrian passport lying next to one of the bodies of the terrorists in Paris now it has transpired that the passport is fake either person used a fake passport or it was planted there either way it poses an interesting question in whose interests is it that people think that this terrorist was a Syrian refugee people have suggested it is Islamic States interest they do not like the pictures of millions of refugees fleeing across to Europe they have presented their caliphate as a refuge for all Muslims and here you have Muslims freeing away from it.

Martin: Europe very reluctant to receive these refugees and when they admitted they admitted under pressure so there was not
not enough screening truly might be terrorist element genuine people laws of deny somebody life.

V/o
After the Russian plane was blasted in Sinai in a few weeks ago , the Russians took action, bombing Syrian Islamic State sites

Bomb Blast

Paula: Russia has a vested interest in stopping the spread of Islamic fundamentalism the Russian President Vladimir Putin is very worried that the spread will come across from the Middle east into Russia and then he has his own problem within Russian with the extremism amongst Chechen’s.

……..In this past week French have also sent in their airforce and even President Obama is talking about sending Special Operation groups into Syria.

Link
There are threats from the West, from Russia...and even China that Islamic state will be crushed...but they are facing an enemy that is extremely difficult to locate and totally committed

Na’eem: I think for those talking about crushing 2 main challenges on is are they willing and able to put tens of thousands of boots on the ground to fight them because you cant fight an enemy like this from the air
Derek: You cant
No you are not going to win and secondly there pools of recruitment need to be dried up How do you dry up that recruitment how do change that discourse way that young Muslims approach Islam ,,,

Martin: Now when you have an enemy not afraid of death even willing to die in battle and death in battle glorified someone cannot be intimidated because the person thinks that is my cause we as counter terrorism fraternity need to review our tactics we need to go back to drawing board to combat new enemy

7 mins 15 sec
